adversarialFindings: THE K5 DEFECT CLASS IS LIVE RIGHT NOW, TODAY. hauska-engine commit 81344ec - the 575x parcel-node PRIMARY KEY sweep fix, committed 2026-08-11T07:23:29-0500 - exists on exactly one disk and nowhere else. Proven three independent ways: (a) git cherry origin/main sweep/fast-write returns '+ 81344ecf...' meaning not-upstream; (b) git show origin/main:packages/engine-core/scripts/write-parcel-node-county.mjs greps 'atom_did' at line 47 only, inside a comment, never in the verify SELECT or the orphan-reconcile SELECT; (c) git log origin/main --grep='PRIMARY KEY' returns nothing. The sibling writers received the identical fix on main via PRs #303/#304, which makes this MORE dangerous, not less: main looks like it has the fix. Anyone reading main would reasonably conclude the parcel-node writer was fixed with its siblings. It was not.

MERGED-BUT-NOT-REALLY, INVERTED. legacy-design-tools presents the opposite illusion and it is just as dangerous. The tree shows gdal.ts at +276/-65, a +91 test file, and two STAGED migration SQLs - a textbook 'uncommitted critical work' signature. It is entirely false. Every one of those files is already on origin/main (git diff --stat origin/main -- <file> is EMPTY; git ls-tree origin/main lists both 0072 and 0073). The local main pointer is 19 commits stale, so git is diffing against a fossil. An agent that 'rescued' this work by committing it would create duplicate migrations 0072/0073 and a migration-numbering collision - the exact failure the upstream commit 45cf0e8b ('renumber observability migrations to 0072/0073 to avoid 0071 NFHL collision') was written to prevent. The correct action is git pull; the intuitive action is actively harmful.

THE 'AHEAD BY N' COLUMN LIES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND I HAD TO CHECK EVERY ONE. Three engine branches advertise large unpushed counts that are pure fiction: feat/phase-d-layer23-cohort claims ahead 77, feat/depth-warm-unified-runner ahead 4, fix/warden-situs-address-column ahead 3 - and all three are 0 commits ahead of origin/main; their tips are merge commits already on main, and the counts are stale tracking-ref artifacts.
